text.content:
Welcome to the Booth, producer. This module turns your table into Celmak's studio. Everything below is GM-only unless it says otherwise.

  1. Open the Producer Console: the broadcast tower button in the Token controls (left toolbar), the button on the ratings board, or the Producer Console macro in the Producer Macros compendium.
  2. Cast the contestants: Console → Ratings → Contestants…. Link each card to a player's actor (or drag the actor onto their card on the board), rename it, or hide companions who are sitting in the Box. The names shown to players are the Russian ones from the art.
  3. Go live: press Show board (or the ON AIR tab at the top of the screen). Every connected player now sees the ratings board.

Import the actors, items and tables you need from the The Hollow Garden: Звёздные Искатели compendium folder; the journal links open them directly.

The board is a small panel that docks to a corner of the screen (each player can move it to another corner with the grid button, drag it, collapse it, or set their own studio volume with the speaker button). It shows two things:

  • Show Rating (1–5), the adventure's own ratings track. It starts at 3. Use the console's quick reasons or the +/– buttons.
  • Fan meters (0–10) for every contestant, shown by name. Portraits change with the fans' mood: crying at 3 or less, cool at 4–6, cheering at 7+. The leader wears the crown; anyone at 2 or less is in the danger zone.

Changing a rating is silent: the board updates and nothing pops up for the players. With Link fan meters to the Show Rating enabled, raising a contestant also nudges the Show Rating the same way (right-click +/– to skip that once).

Announcements need your approval

When the Show Rating reaches 5 or 1, the GM-only Ratings Announcement desk opens with a suggested message in Russian. Edit the headline and text, choose the sticker, sound and effects, optionally award a Trinket (peak) or pick Celmak's response (escalation), and set the rating to reset to. Players see nothing unless you press Broadcast. The same desk is on the console's Ratings tab (Escalation…, Ratings peak…, Custom announcement…) and on each contestant's megaphone button. Turn the automatic offer off in module settings if you prefer.

Linking actors

Drag an actor from the Actors sidebar onto a contestant's card on the board, or onto their row in Contestants…, or pick it from the list there. A chain icon marks linked cards; click the portrait to open the sheet. Trinkets go to the linked actor's sheet and the honeypot desk rolls from it.

Celmak's schedule is fixed, but the audience doesn't need to know that. Games → Spin the Episode Wheel opens the rigging desk:

  • Tick which episodes are already done (they drop off the wheel).
  • Choose where the wheel will land. The default is the next episode on Celmak's schedule.
  • Pick a spin length and press Spin. Every client sees the same wheel slow down and land on your choice, with ticks, a drumroll and a fanfare.

When it lands you get a GM chat card with a link to the episode's journal page and a Roll title card button.

• Soundboard: each cue plays a sound for everyone and pops up a sticker of the host. Shift-click previews it only for you.
  • Stickers: pop any of the host's 28 stickers silently.
  • Celmak says: pick a persona (Host, Critic, Lover, Child), type a line or draw a random one, and it appears as a broadcast caption with the matching sticker.
  • Title cards: episode openers, Commercial Break (intermission; optionally −1 rating; plays adverts if they are switched on), Previously On…, and the Season Finale.

Each player can lower the module's sound volume, turn off stickers, or reduce motion in their own module settings.

The console's Effects tab plays full-screen effects for everyone. Shift-click any button to preview it only for you. Set Duration to override how long an effect lasts; Stop all effects ends every running effect, looped sound and advert for everyone.

  • Malfunctions: Blackout (lights die, red emergency beacon, power returns), TV static, No signal (colour bars and test tone), The Gap glitch, Hologram desync (tearing bands and colour fringing on the map), Short circuit (spark showers), Electric arcs (good for the Prize Sentinel's nanite field), Buffering…, Gravity failure (the whole view tilts and sways), System crash (error screen, memory dump, reboot), Red alert (klaxon and beacons) and Lockdown (blast doors).
  • Studio: neon signs (АПЛОДИСМЕНТЫ with applause, ТИШИНА В СТУДИИ, or your own text and colour), an on-screen Countdown with a buzzer, a Spotlight that finds your selected (or targeted) tokens, Celmak's Camera feed, a Breaking news crawl with your text, confetti and screen shake.
  • Garden & scenes: the four seasons of the Garden episode (each with its particles, sound and, optionally, its rules line), Stage smoke, a Drift jump, the Dimensional lock pulse, and the two Mood Gas vents (which roll the d6 table and post the DCs).

Macros can call any effect: game.modules.get("hollow-garden").api.effect("blackout", { duration: 8 }). api.effects() lists the names.

Celmak's channel has sponsors. The Ads tab holds eleven in-world adverts (Аплодин, Чистый нос, Газ настроения «Домашний набор», Стенд-ин™, Гарден-Кредит, Садовые услуги «Колосс», Отель «Зелёная комната», Манекен-компаньон «Идеал», Карточки «Спойлер!», Парфюм «Ничто» and Энергетик «ДРИФТ»), each about 15–25 seconds with its own jingle, pack shot, price sticker and fine print. Testimonials star a random contestant who is on stage.

  • Play commercials after the break card switches them on or off. The same toggle sits next to the Commercial break button on the Broadcast tab.
  • Choose how many adverts run per break, whether they play in random order (no repeats until the pool runs out) or in turn, and whether the «Мы снова в эфире!» card follows.
  • Tick the adverts that are in rotation. The eye button previews one only for you; the tower button airs it immediately for everyone.

During a break you get Skip and End break buttons in the corner of your screen; players don't.

Audience vote: enter a question and up to four options, then set the rigged percentages (or pick a winner and let the console invent believable numbers). Players watch a live vote with a countdown before the result is revealed.

Everything the players see (board, title cards, captions, wheel, votes, public chat cards) is in Russian; this guide and the console stay in English.

Honeypot check: when someone reads one of the Garden's machines with Knowledge (engineering), open Games → Honeypot check. Roll from the linked actor's sheet or type in the total and the natural d20. The console sorts the result into the bands (61+ real answer; 60 or less with a natural 1–10 is an amusing fake (the whisper has a Celmak laughs, +1 button if you want it public); 11–20 is a detrimental fake) and whispers you the table result. Players only see what you tell them.
